name: Costume Jewellery
summary: Jewels made to go with a dress, not to hold value. They are glass pearls, paste, gilt metal, Bakelite and chrome, worn in ropes and clusters by day and night, and chosen for the look.

philosophy.core_thesis: A jewel is an accessory to the outfit: it need not be real, because the effect counts for more than the value.
design_principles: Make the piece from cheap, bright materials: glass pearl, paste, gilt brass, celluloid, Bakelite and chrome.
Wear the piece in quantity: a rope of 120 to 200 cm of glass pearls, or six bracelets on one arm.
Copy a real jewel in size and form, then change one thing, such as a cross, a coin or a colour. The change makes it read as a joke on wealth.
Mix real and false pieces on the same person, and make no secret of which is which.
Change the jewel each season to match the new colour and cut of the dress.
Plate the base metal with gold, silver or chrome by the electric bath, and keep the plate thin and bright.
Cast, stamp or mould the parts in large runs from one die, and sell them at a low price.
Make a large piece: a brooch of 6 to 10 cm or a cuff of 4 to 6 cm width.
anti_patterns: A single small precious stone in a plain frame
Hidden clasps and quiet, discreet size
Hand-made, one-off pieces for a collector

silhouette.shape: A large, bold, easy piece: a long rope of pearls, a wide cuff, a clip brooch or a pair of button earrings.
silhouette.line: Round and rope-like, or a block of colour; shapes taken from coins, crosses, flowers and shells.
silhouette.fit: Worn in layers, in ropes over a knit or a suit, pinned on a lapel, clipped on a collar or an ear.
silhouette.proportion: A rope of pearls is 120 to 200 cm long. A cuff is 4 to 6 cm wide. A brooch is 6 to 10 cm across.
rules: Hang two or three ropes of pearls in different lengths over a plain dress.
Match the colour of the jewel to the dress or to the season.
Clip a large brooch on the lapel or the hat.
Wear a wide cuff in gilt metal with a bright cabochon over the sleeve.

fabrics.rule: Make the jewel from cheap, bright and strong materials, and choose each one for its colour and its shine.

methods: paste stones in glued or claw settings
moulded and carved Bakelite and celluloid
poured glass set in a metal frame
construction.closures: A simple spring clasp, a clip back, a screw back or a pin; a hook and chain on a necklace.
construction.details: A cross, a coin, a flower or a shell as the form; large cabochons; a hook closure that shows on the front.

surface.pattern: Ropes, clusters and borders of beads, with a repeat that the die gives.
surface.gloss: High and bright: chrome and glass at 80 to 100 GU; Bakelite at 60 to 80 GU.
surface.wear: The thin plate wears at the edge and shows the brass; the style accepts this, and the piece is cheap to replace.

palette.strategy: Bright, flat colours chosen for the dress: black, white, red and green, with a gilt or a chrome ground.

making.scale: Workshops and factories, from the French glass houses to the American mass makers, with runs of thousands from one die.
making.signs: Visible seam lines, a thin plate, uniform stones and a stamped maker's name on the back.

pieces.form: Long rope of glass pearls with a knot
Large paste brooch in the form of a flower
Wide gilt cuff with a cross
Chrome-plated pendant on a chain of links

positive: layers of necklaces over a plain dress

canonical_works.work: Maltese cross cuff bracelet for Chanel

evidence.title: Chanel pearl necklace LOT 4264 AW Auctions

emotion.target_response: A light, witty and modern feeling: the viewer sees a joke on wealth and the pleasure of a new look.

use_cases: a fashion shoot with jewels that match the clothes
costume design for a 1920s or 1930s film
an image prompt for bold fashion jewellery
avoid_when: the brief wants real stones and a fine finish
the brief wants a discreet, one-off jewel

modifiers.how: Replace the paste and the chrome with diamonds and platinum, and keep the bold geometry.
Use large cabochon stones in gilt or gold, with ribbons and bows, and keep the bold size.

ornament_level.note: Costume jewellery runs from one plain rope to a full cluster of pieces.
